- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent range.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) and price is falling, model often overcorrects downward — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend — apply +1.5%–3% upward adjustment to early forecast peaks.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each day beyond 10–15 days into the forecast window.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and price is near recent high/low, model tends to “stick” — apply smoothing filter or use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias in final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish or stable.
